ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $CD$ is the bisector of $\angle ACB$. Extend $CD$ to point $E$ such that $DE = \frac{1}{2}CD$. Connect $BE$. If $AC = 2BC$ and the area of $\triangle BDE$ is $1$, what is the area of $\triangle ABC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\[
\textbf{Solution:} \text{As shown in the figure, draw } DG \perp AC \text{ at } G, \text{ and } DH \perp CB \text{ at } H, \\
\because DE = \frac{1}{2}CD, \text{ and the area of } \triangle BDE \text{ is 1,} \\
\therefore S\triangle BCD = 2S\triangle BDE = 2, \\
\because CD \text{ is the angle bisector of } \angle ACB, DH \perp CB, \text{ and } DG \perp AC, \\
\therefore DG = DH, \\
\because AC = 2BC, S_{\triangle ACD} = \frac{1}{2}AC \cdot GD, S_{\triangle BCD} = \frac{1}{2}BC \cdot DH, \\
\therefore S\triangle ACD = 2S\triangle BCD, \\
\therefore S\triangle ACD = 4, \\
\therefore S\triangle ABC = S\triangle ACD + S\triangle BCD = 4 + 2 = \boxed{6}.
\]

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description first: In the attached diagram, A, D, and B lie on the same horizontal segment AB with D between A and B. Point C is above AB, and the line through C and D is extended past D to point E below AB, so C, D, and E are collinear. Segment BE is drawn, forming the shaded triangle BDE. The full triangle is ABC, with CD drawn from C to D. Reasoning following the assigned method: Since C, D, and E are collinear, triangles BCD and BDE use bases CD and DE on the same line CDE. They also share the same altitude from B to line CDE. Therefore their areas are proportional to their bases. Given DE = (1/2)CD and [BDE] = 1, we get [BCD] = 2[BDE] = 2. Because CD bisects angle ACB and D lies on AB, by the angle-bisector theorem, AD:DB = AC:BC. Given AC = 2BC, we have AD:DB = 2:1. Triangles ACD and BCD have bases AD and DB on the same line AB and share the same altitude from C to AB, so their areas are in the same ratio as their bases: [ACD]:[BCD] = AD:DB = 2:1. Since [BCD] = 2, it follows that [ACD] = 4. Thus [ABC] = [ACD] + [BCD] = 4 + 2 = 6.
